title: Hip Fracture in an Older Adult
description: Relieve pain without NSAIDs, operate on the day of or after admission, match the implant to the fracture pattern, and mobilize the next day within an orthogeriatric program.
objectives: Provide early analgesia, including nerve blocks, without delaying surgery
Time surgery to the day of or after admission, correcting comorbidities in parallel
Choose arthroplasty, fixation, or nailing by fracture pattern and the patient's function
Mobilize on day one with full weight bearing, inside an orthogeriatric program

references.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Hip fracture: management. Clinical guideline CG124. London: NICE; 2011 (updated 2023).
HIP ATTACK Investigators. Accelerated surgery versus standard care in hip fracture (HIP ATTACK): an international, randomised, controlled trial. Lancet. 2020;395(10225):698-708.
HEALTH Investigators; Bhandari M, Einhorn TA, Guyatt G, et al. Total Hip Arthroplasty or Hemiarthroplasty for Hip Fracture. N Engl J Med. 2019;381(23):2199-2208.
Guay J, Kopp S. Peripheral nerve blocks for hip fractures in adults. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2020;11(11):CD001159.

start.text: An 82-year-old woman fell at home and cannot bear weight. Her right leg is shortened and externally rotated. She lives alone, walks outdoors with a stick, and manages all her own daily activities. She is mildly confused tonight.

analgesia.text: Hip X-ray confirms a fracture. Which belong in her first hours?

options.label: Immediate analgesia, reassessed within 30 minutes
Regular paracetamol, with opioids if needed
A peripheral nerve block if pain persists or to limit opioids
Assess her for cognitive impairment and delirium
An NSAID to spare opioids
A nerve block, so surgery can wait until pain is controlled

analgesia.feedback: NICE CG124: offer immediate analgesia, including to people with cognitive impairment, and reassess within 30 minutes. Give paracetamol every 6 hours, adding opioids if needed; NSAIDs are not recommended. Consider a nerve block if pain persists or to limit opioids, but never as a substitute for early surgery. Look for cognitive impairment and delirium from admission. Cochrane 2020: nerve blocks cut pain on movement and acute confusion (RR 0.67; NNT 12).

timing.text: Her potassium is 3.1 mmol/L and she has a new murmur. When do you operate?

options.label: After a formal echocardiogram and cardiology review next week
options.feedback: NICE CG124: operate on the day of, or the day after, admission. Identify and treat correctable comorbidities immediately so that surgery is not delayed.

options.label: Emergency surgery tonight, within 6 hours of diagnosis
options.feedback: In HIP ATTACK, surgery within a median of 6 hours did not lower 90-day mortality (9% vs 10%) or major complications (22% in both) compared with standard care, which took a median of 24 hours. NICE CG124 recommends surgery on the day of or after admission, on a planned trauma list.

options.label: On the day of or the day after admission, correcting the potassium and assessing the murmur without delaying surgery
options.feedback: NICE CG124: operate on the day of, or the day after, admission on a planned trauma list, treating correctable comorbidities such as electrolyte imbalance immediately so they do not delay surgery. HIP ATTACK found no benefit from accelerating surgery to about 6 hours.

intracapsular.text: The fracture is a displaced intracapsular (femoral neck) fracture. She is fit for surgery and should stay independent beyond 2 years. Which operation?

options.label: Cannulated screw fixation to preserve her own hip
options.feedback: NICE CG124: offer replacement arthroplasty, total hip replacement or hemiarthroplasty, for a displaced intracapsular fracture.

options.label: Cemented arthroplasty, considering total hip replacement because she walks outdoors with a stick and is expected to stay independent
options.feedback: NICE CG124: offer arthroplasty for a displaced intracapsular fracture and use cemented implants. Consider total hip replacement over hemiarthroplasty for people who walk outdoors with no more than a stick, are fit for it, and are expected to stay independent beyond 2 years (2023). In HEALTH, total hip arthroplasty did not reduce secondary procedures (7.9% vs 8.3%). Function was modestly better, but dislocation was more common (4.7% vs 2.4%).

options.label: Uncemented hemiarthroplasty to shorten the operation
options.feedback: NICE CG124: use cemented implants for arthroplasty after hip fracture. For someone with her mobility and outlook, total hip replacement should also be considered.

trochanteric.text: The fracture is trochanteric, above the lesser trochanter and not reverse oblique. Which implant?

options.label: Intramedullary nail
options.feedback: NICE CG124: use an extramedullary implant such as a sliding hip screw, in preference to an intramedullary nail, for trochanteric fractures above and including the lesser trochanter (except reverse oblique).

options.label: Sliding hip screw
options.feedback: NICE CG124: use extramedullary implants such as a sliding hip screw rather than an intramedullary nail for trochanteric fractures above and including the lesser trochanter, except reverse oblique patterns.

subtrochanteric.text: The fracture is subtrochanteric. Which implant?

options.label: Intramedullary nail
options.feedback: NICE CG124: use an intramedullary nail to treat a subtrochanteric fracture.

options.label: Sliding hip screw
options.feedback: NICE CG124: subtrochanteric fractures are treated with an intramedullary nail. The sliding hip screw is for trochanteric fractures at or above the lesser trochanter.

rehab.text: Surgery goes well. Which belong in her postoperative plan?

options.label: Physiotherapy assessment and mobilization on the day after surgery
Full weight bearing without restriction
An orthogeriatric hip fracture program, including falls and bone health
Bed rest for a week to protect the repair
Touch weight bearing only for 6 weeks

rehab.feedback: NICE CG124: operate so that people can fully weight bear without restriction immediately after surgery. Offer physiotherapy assessment and mobilization on the day after surgery, then at least daily. From admission, offer an orthogeriatric Hip Fracture Programme with rapid optimization, rehabilitation goals, and links to falls prevention and bone health services.

fail_analgesia.text: Guideline Deviation: Analgesia or delirium care off guideline.

fail_delay.text: Guideline Deviation: Surgery delayed beyond the day after admission.

fail_rushed.text: Guideline Deviation: Out-of-hours surgery without evidence of benefit.

fail_implant.text: Management Error: Implant does not match the fracture pattern.

success.text: Case Complete: Timely surgery with the right implant and early mobilization.
